codemap:
rulebook.md — the session rulebook the issue orders compressed; test-repo.sh keys cases on its material-terms list, its Issue Mode numbered step and the phrase 'small or obvious'
GEMINI.md — must stay byte-identical to rulebook.md; today a symlink to it, so it follows rulebook.md unless the change breaks the link (a cmp case in test-repo.sh guards the identity)
agents/implementer.md — agent page to compress; test-repo.sh checks it names the codemap
agents/planner.md — agent page to compress; test-repo.sh holds it as the sole owner of the phrase 'chain depth' among agent pages and shipped skills
agents/researcher.md — agent page to compress; test-repo.sh keys cases on its phrases (per-criterion go-red case, 'production change', the breaks/unbreakable templates, 'says so and why')
agents/reviewer.md — agent page to compress, the largest; test-repo.sh checks it points at the mutation standard without restating it
agents/test-author.md — agent page to compress
skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md — skill page to compress; test-repo.sh keys on '## The mutation standard', sole ownership of 'counts as tested', 'push the commit', 'already committed', 'backlog.mjs'
skills/argus/SKILL.md — skill page to compress
skills/grill/SKILL.md — skill page to compress
skills/retro/SKILL.md — skill page to compress
.claude/rules/agents.md — rules page to compress; deliberately outside test-repo.sh's cross-file duplicate checks, and a case requires it to point at .claude/rules/authoring.md
.claude/rules/authoring.md — rules page to compress; test-repo.sh parses its table rows and its paths: frontmatter (skills/** and agents/**)
workflows/agile-loop.js — the only workflow artifact; its dispatched prompt and schema-description strings are the workflow's rule text the issue calls a workflow page, and several test-repo.sh cases grep this file
test-repo.sh — re-key every case whose grep keys on wording the compression changed so it still turns red when its rule is removed; delete no case

increments.title: Compress the five agent pages
increments.goal: Every page under agents/ says all it said in fewer words, and the suite still guards it.
criteria: Each of agents/implementer.md, agents/planner.md, agents/researcher.md, agents/reviewer.md and agents/test-author.md is shorter than it was, measured in words.
Everything the old text of these pages required is still required, and everything it forbade is still forbidden.
Each page states each rule once, in short imperative sentences of common words; history, anecdotes and self-justification are gone, and no reason runs past one sentence.
Each page's role, audience, file location and English are unchanged.
Every test-repo.sh case keyed on wording these pages changed is re-keyed to the new wording and still turns red when its rule is removed; no case is deleted.
bash test.sh exits 0.
increments.note: First because it is the largest group with the densest wording-keyed test coverage: the run learns the compress-and-re-key pattern here.

increments.title: Compress the workflow's dispatched rule text
increments.goal: The rule text workflows/agile-loop.js hands agents is compressed, with the workflow's behavior intact.
criteria: The prompt and schema-description strings in workflows/agile-loop.js — the rule text agents receive — are shorter than they were, measured in words.
Everything the old strings required is still required, and everything they forbade is still forbidden; each instruction is stated once.
The compressed strings use short imperative sentences in common words; no reason runs past one sentence, and history and self-justification are gone.
Only string content changes: the workflow's code paths and behavior are unchanged, and the file's role, audience, location and English are unchanged.
Every test-repo.sh case keyed on wording this file changed is re-keyed to the new wording and still turns red when its rule is removed; no case is deleted.
bash test.sh exits 0.
increments.note: Second because it carries this run's own unknown: rule text embedded in code. If research shows these strings are not what the issue means by a workflow page, that comes back as a codemap correction and the increment is re-cut or dropped.

increments.title: Compress the four skill pages
increments.goal: Every SKILL.md under skills/ says all it said in fewer words, and the suite still guards it.
criteria: Each of skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md, skills/argus/SKILL.md, skills/grill/SKILL.md and skills/retro/SKILL.md is shorter than it was, measured in words.
Everything the old text of these pages required is still required, and everything it forbade is still forbidden.
Each page states each rule once, in short imperative sentences of common words; history, anecdotes and self-justification are gone, and no reason runs past one sentence.
Each page's role, audience, file location, frontmatter contract and English are unchanged.
Every test-repo.sh case keyed on wording these pages changed is re-keyed to the new wording and still turns red when its rule is removed; no case is deleted.
bash test.sh exits 0.

increments.title: Compress the rulebook and the pages under .claude/rules/
increments.goal: rulebook.md (with its GEMINI.md mirror) and both pages under .claude/rules/ say all they said in fewer words.
criteria: Each of rulebook.md, .claude/rules/agents.md and .claude/rules/authoring.md is shorter than it was, measured in words.
Everything the old text of these documents required is still required, and everything it forbade is still forbidden.
Each document states each rule once, in short imperative sentences of common words; history, anecdotes and self-justification are gone, and no reason runs past one sentence.
Each document's role, audience, file location, frontmatter and English are unchanged.
GEMINI.md is byte-identical to rulebook.md after the change.
Every test-repo.sh case keyed on wording these documents changed is re-keyed to the new wording and still turns red when its rule is removed; no case is deleted.
bash test.sh exits 0.
increments.note: Last because it is the smallest group and the pattern is proven by then; GEMINI.md is a symlink today, so the mirror holds unless an edit breaks the link.

steps.label: decompose

rulings: Treat the dispatched prompt and schema-description strings in workflows/agile-loop.js as the issue's workflow page, because workflows/ holds no markdown and those strings are the only workflow rule text agents receive; wrong costs one reverted increment.

Exclude README.md and every CLAUDE.md (skills/, skills/agent-brief/assets/, hooks/, tools/*) from the scope, because the issue's scope list is closed and names none of them; wrong costs a follow-up issue to compress them.
return.summary: Cut into four increments, one per rule-document class, each carrying the issue's quality criteria scoped to its own files plus the re-keying of the test-repo.sh cases its wording changes, and each closing with bash test.sh at exit 0 — a single all-documents increment was rejected as one unreviewable 15-file diff, and a separate re-keying increment was rejected because it would leave the suite red between increments. All four run full: every document group is dense with wording-keyed test-repo.sh cases and the compression wording is left to decide. Criterion mapping: compress each agent page → agent-pages; compress each workflow page → workflow-text; compress each skill page → skill-pages; compress rulebook.md and each page under .claude/rules/ → session-rules; keep GEMINI.md byte-identical to rulebook.md → session-rules; the cross-cutting criteria (shorter in words, keep every binding rule, state each rule once, short imperative sentences, drop history with reasons of at most one sentence, role/audience/location unchanged, English, re-key test-repo.sh cases without deleting any, bash test.sh exits 0) are restated inside each increment scoped to its own documents, so each scoped instance lands in exactly one increment; leave docs/issues/ untouched binds every increment and no increment touches it.

steps.prompt:
Issue directory: docs/issues/2026-08-16-compress-the-rules
Open the run state for docs/issues/2026-08-16-compress-the-rules/issue.md: map the issue against the codebase, decide the cut, and write both into docs/issues/2026-08-16-compress-the-rules/backlog.json with the `init` subcommand of the backlog helper your shared brief names, with workflow "agile-loop" and the whole codemap in the payload's `codemap` field.
This run works at most 8 increments, so a cut that needs more than that is a cut that is too fine.
Announce this step before you begin it and record it before you return, the way your shared brief describes, with the backlog helper it names:
  - `start docs/issues/2026-08-16-compress-the-rules/backlog.json - decompose <the prompt file>` — the prompt you were given, verbatim and whole, in a file outside the repository.
  - `record docs/issues/2026-08-16-compress-the-rules/backlog.json - decompose <the return file> <the prompt file>` — your return, in a file outside the repository, with that same prompt file. Commit it with your work and push the commit.
The fields your return carries, and your page says what each one holds:
  - `questions`
  - `rulings`
  - `summary`
